# Configuration keys

Source: `config/harness-knobs.json`.

Use `provenant config schema` for effective values, or `provenant config schema --all` for all editable fields and their effective values; the [advanced reference](config-keys-all.md) documents host policy and tuning.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `profile` | balanced | Select balanced or economy defaults |
| `lanes.max_concurrency` | 8 | Default number of lanes one batch runs at once when any lane in it writes a worktree, resolved from the profile. An explicit dispatch concurrency wins. |
| `lanes.max_concurrency_read_only` | 16 | Default number of lanes one batch runs at once when no lane in it writes a worktree, resolved from the profile. A lanes.max_concurrency you set yourself also caps it unless you set this knob too. An explicit dispatch concurrency wins. |
| `lanes.max_depth` | 2 | Maximum nested lane depth, including the first dispatched lane. |
| `lanes.silence_seconds` | 1800 | Mark a provider observation silent after this many seconds without output or CPU progress; never kill it for silence. |
| `lanes.slot_wait_seconds` | 7200 | Most time in total that a lane's build-slot waits keep off its wall-clock deadline. Beyond it the wall deadline runs while the lane waits, so a stuck lane cannot wait forever. 0 keeps no waiting off the deadline. |
| `lanes.context_handoff_tokens` | 0 | Context size, in tokens one provider call sent, at which the host stops a writer so a fresh attempt continues from its handoff on the same worktree. The stop settles as a declared stop and uses the graph's one automatic continuation; commits and uncommitted edits stay in place. 0 is off. Suggested setting 200000. Only providers that report each call's context (Claude) are stopped; others keep today's behaviour. |
| `lanes.publish` | true | Let every lane with open network, read-only lanes included, use the host's gh login, a git credential helper and gh to push their own branch and read or update issues and pull requests. |
| `lanes.local_cargo` | all | Which cargo subcommands a lane may run locally, enforced in the lane's cargo shim for every provider. all runs everything; check allows only `cargo check` (and subcommands that do not compile, such as fmt and metadata); none refuses every compiling command, `cargo check` included. A refused command exits non-zero with one line saying CI runs it. Set per run with --knob lanes.local_cargo=check, per graph node with `attempt.local_cargo`, or for the host under [knobs]. |
| `lanes.isolation` | private | Whether an unpinned read-only graph node reads its bound checkout live (shared). A read-only lane pinned to a commit always gets an immutable source view, under every setting. Writers always keep one writer per worktree, so shared is refused on a writer node. Set per graph node with `attempt.isolation` or the `light` preset (`attempt.preset`),. |
| `lanes.supervision` | standard | minimal marks a silent provider only after the longest silence interval (one hour) instead of lanes.silence_seconds. Set per graph node with `attempt.supervision` or the `light` preset. |
| `lanes.receipts` | delivery | Delivery requested by a writer always runs and records its outcome. Set per graph node with `attempt.receipts` or the `light` preset. |
| `routing.exclude` | empty | Keep each listed provider (claude), account (label, entry or adapter/key) or exact model (adapter/id) out of named-route pools for every task. A standing list; `--exclude` and a graph's list are added to it, not substituted for it. A pinned `--model` is never affected. |
| `routing.graph_exclude` | empty | The exclusion list a graph passes to each node it launches, set from graph routing policy. Same selectors as `routing.exclude`; refusals and `--explain` name the graph as the source. |
| `fabric.accept_handoff` | false | Let a Fabric peer start a Claude session on this host through a session hand-off. |
| `usage.project_attribution` | false | Include the existing project identifier in local usage events. |
| `domains.run.writer_token_budget` | 500000 | Tokens a writer attempt may use, from the fresh usage its provider reports, before it is ended so a continuation can pick it up. The host then attempts to commit and publish the lane's work; it does not when custody is not absent, when a merge, cherry-pick, revert or rebase is in progress, or when the commit fails, and settlement notes say which. 0 turns the budget off. Cache reads do not count. Enforced for Claude from live usage and for Codex at completed-turn boundaries. Codex reports usage in turn.completed frames, so the host can stop it after a turn passes the budget but cannot interrupt a turn mid-flight. Other providers without live usage are not enforced. Launch warnings or receipt notes say so. Current lane adapters cannot receive a live steer: the 90% warning records an unsupported control receipt. After custody is absent the host attempts a bounded commit only when no Git operation is in progress; an in-progress merge is preserved for stopped-merge handling, a cherry-pick, revert or rebase in progress is left uncommitted, and a skipped or failed commit is reported without replacing the budget outcome. Time queued for a build slot does not count towards the wall-clock deadline, up to lanes.slot_wait_seconds in total. The source (run, project, host or default) is shown with the budget. |
| `domains.pr.land.integration` | batch | Integration strategy. |
| `domains.pr.land.batch_size` | 8 | Maximum pull requests in a batch. |
| `domains.pr.land.gate.checks` | ci-status | Required candidate checks. |
| `domains.pr.land.gate.timeout_seconds` | 3600 | Candidate gate timeout. |
| `domains.pr.land.local_gate.mode` | warn | Fast pre-push gate behaviour. |
| `domains.pr.land.local_gate.commands` | empty | Fast pre-push command plan. |
| `domains.fabric.graph.limits.nodes` | 512 | Graph nodes limit. |
| `domains.fabric.graph.limits.expansion_depth` | 64 | Longest dependency chain in edges, root nodes at depth 0, and deepest composite nesting a graph may expand to. Graph documents cannot raise it. |
| `domains.fabric.graph.limits.concurrency` | 0 | Graph concurrency limit. Zero uses host lane caps. |
| `domains.fabric.lanes.max_concurrent_builds` | max(1, min(cores / cargo_build_jobs, GiB of RAM / 6)) | A build throttle, not a hard cap: cargo builds, tests, checks and lints that a lane's cargo shim runs at once across the host and every project that shares the state directory. Lanes are not capped by it; a command that compiles waits for a free slot. Direct ~/.cargo/bin/cargo, rustc and non-cargo builds are not gated. |
| `domains.fabric.lanes.build_wait_minutes` | 30 | Minutes a build waits for a build slot or another build's Cargo lock before it gives up with an error. |
| `providers.{provider}.update` | true | Run the detected native updater in a detached one-shot worker scheduled by quota events. Provider preparation briefly shares the update lock; running lanes do not hold it. If all candidates are updating, dispatch waits at most --wait (capped at 30 seconds), then uses the installed version. false opts out; {command: [program, argument, ...]} overrides the updater directly without a shell. |
| `providers.{provider}.runtime_deadline_seconds` | unset | Cap on the wall-clock runtime of any lane on this provider. A dispatch's own --provider-timeout applies when it is shorter. At the deadline the provider is stopped and the attempt settles as timed_out, whatever the host did meanwhile, including sleeping. |
| `gc.graph_checkpoint_days` | 90 | Retain terminal graph checkpoints for at least this many days after their last save |
